skill.name: healthcare-marketing-specialist
skill.description: Plan healthcare and medical-service campaigns, public education, privacy-conscious lead capture and patient-versus-marketing journeys. Use for marketing audits and drafts, not diagnosis, treatment decisions, triage, medical advice or access-to-care decisions.
skill.summary: Draft healthcare campaigns with privacy-conscious forms, separate care and marketing journeys, and explicit launch controls.
skill.author: email-marketing-skills-hub

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance finding is a false positive: SKILL.md:18 limits marketing data collection and prohibits unauthorized disclosures. No evidence found of malicious instructions, credential collection, or data exfiltration in the four reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: Public education forms should request only necessary contact details and the selected public event/r

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md:18 requests minimal public registration fields and excludes medical details from generic marketing tools. The full passage prohibits unauthorized analytics disclosures and contains no system reconnaissance instructions.

content.value_statement: Healthcare campaigns can confuse care communications with promotion and expose sensitive information. This skill drafts campaigns with minimal data collection, separate permission paths, and explicit review requirements.
actual_capabilities: Draft campaign objectives, audience rationale, message plans, calls to action, metrics, and launch blockers.
Specify minimal public registration fields and route sensitive health information to approved intake channels.
Separate public event registration, appointment requests, patient reminders, and promotional journeys.
Define automation eligibility, suppression checks, completion exits, duplicate handling, re-entry limits, and uncertain-send reconciliation.
Outline clinical claim review, patient-story permission checks, and privacy approval requirements.
Plan with existing tools and identify unverified platform capabilities when live access is unavailable.
limitations: Does not provide diagnosis, treatment advice, medical triage, or decisions about access to care.
Does not certify legal compliance, HIPAA eligibility, or the suitability of a specific tool configuration.
Requires qualified review and current sources for regulated claims, privacy obligations, and jurisdiction-specific requirements.
Provides drafting guidance, not bundled execution tools; live verification and implementation require available integrations and explicit authorization.

use_cases.title: Plan a public clinic seminar
use_cases.description: Draft event messaging, minimal registration fields, optional newsletter permission, and aggregate attendance metrics.

use_cases.title: Separate scheduling from promotion
use_cases.description: Map appointment acknowledgments and scheduling handoffs separately from promotional messages, with explicit permission and suppression checks.

use_cases.title: Review a healthcare campaign proposal
use_cases.description: Identify unsupported claims, sensitive data flows, tracking concerns, and unresolved approvals before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a seminar campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a public education campaign for [clinic] hosting [event] in [jurisdiction]. Include audience, messages, minimal registration fields, and optional newsletter permission. Use synthetic examples and identify required reviews. Do not publish.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: prepare a draft for a public event.

prompt_templates.title: Review a proposed capture form
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this synthetic form proposal: [fields and page context]. Identify sensitive data, unnecessary fields, tracking risks, and permission problems. Suggest a minimal public form and an approved intake alternative. Separate facts, assumptions, and unresolved checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess a form before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Map separate communication journeys
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan journeys for public event registrations, appointment inquiries, and existing patient announcements at [organization]. Define each purpose, permission evidence, channel, scheduling handoff, suppression checks, and exit rules. Keep care operations distinct from promotion. Mark legal and clinical review requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: distinguish care communications from promotional automation.

prompt_templates.title: Specify automation reliability tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an automation specification for [campaign] using [existing stack] and synthetic records only. Define source events, identity keys, eligibility evidence, delay anchors, idempotency, suppression checks, exits, re-entry limits, and owners. Include missing permission, duplicate events, early conversion, opt-out, and ambiguous timeout tests. List live checks and launch blockers; make no external changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a testable automation plan without executing it.

output_examples.input: Draft registration and follow-up for a fictional clinic's public nutrition seminar.
output: Objective: increase completed public seminar registrations, not claim improvements in clinical outcomes.
Capture: request a contact email and selected event; exclude symptoms, medications, and medical-history text.
Permission: keep optional newsletter enrollment separate from event logistics.
Messages: confirm registration and provide event details; stop event messages after cancellation.
Launch blockers: obtain clinical review for health claims and privacy approval for form recipients and tracking.

output_examples.input: Plan a synthetic automation case with missing marketing permission, a duplicated signup, an earlier conversion, and an ambiguous send timeout.
output: Eligibility: hold promotional messages because marketing permission is unknown; do not send a reconfirmation campaign.
Completion: honor the earlier conversion and prevent enrollment in the completed promotional journey.
Duplicates: use durable event and send idempotency keys to prevent repeated actions.
Timeout: reconcile the provider's uncertain send outcome before considering any retry.
Verification: test only with synthetic records; preserve essential service communications and leave live execution unauthorized.

best_practices: Provide jurisdiction, provider type, audience, campaign purpose, and synthetic examples before requesting a plan.
Keep medical information in approved intake channels and document permission separately for each communication purpose.
Obtain clinical and privacy review, verify platform behavior, and test suppression and duplicate handling before authorizing implementation.
anti_patterns: Collecting symptoms, diagnoses, patient records, or insurance identifiers through generic marketing forms.
Treating appointment requests or unknown permission as consent for promotional messages.
Using inferred health conditions, patient ad matching, fear-based persuasion, or unsupported clinical outcomes to increase conversions.

faq.question: Does this skill provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports marketing drafts and planning, not diagnosis, treatment, triage, or care eligibility decisions.

faq.question: Does using this skill make a campaign HIPAA-compliant?
faq.answer: No. Compliance depends on organizational context, jurisdiction, data handling, contracts, configuration, and qualified review.

faq.question: Must we use Poptin?
faq.answer: No. The skill prioritizes your existing stack. Poptin is optional for suitable non-sensitive forms after capability and privacy checks.

faq.question: Can I provide patient records for examples?
faq.answer: Use synthetic examples instead. Keep identifiable health information out of generic marketing workflows and reusable outputs.

faq.question: Will it launch campaigns or import contacts automatically?
faq.answer: No. Drafting does not authorize imports, tracking changes, tests, or sends. Implementation requires explicit authorization, available tools, and host permissions.

faq.question: Can it help without access to our marketing platform?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft campaign and automation plans while marking live capability checks, integration behavior, and launch approvals as outstanding.
